title: Reference prompt collections lifecycle and change traceability
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Overview:
We need a robust lifecycle and governance model for "trusted reference prompt collections" used by our continuous evaluation pipelines so that config/model changes trigger reliable, auditable quality regressions. This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for: curation, immutable snapshotting/versioning, permissioning (RBAC + ACL), change traceability, CI/CD gating integration, and Console UX for managing these collections.

Motivation:
- Multiple regressions in the last quarter were caused by silent config changes that were not linked to an eval suite. Teams cannot consistently pin a reference collection to a rollout, nor can they see who changed which prompts and why.
- We must reduce false positives/negatives in regression detection by coupling stable, curated collections with metadata (provenance, sampling strategy, expected distribution).

Scope / Deliverables:
1) Data model and storage: a canonical representation for a reference collection with fields: name, description, owner (team + steward), tag set, intended distribution, immutable snapshot id (digest), human-readable version, created_by, created_at, and changelog message. Snapshots are stored as immutable artifacts (S3 + digest) and referenced by id from eval runs.
2) Versioning & immutability: every save creates a new immutable snapshot. Edits create a new version; we do NOT modify snapshots in-place. Provide a compact semantic versioning rule for minor/major dataset changes and an API to compare two versions.
3) Access control: project-level RBAC + collection-level ACLs. Roles: owner, steward, reviewer, reader. Owners can set required approvers for changes. Integrate with SSO/SAML groups and Console UI for assignment.
4) Curation workflow: draft -> review -> approved -> published. Reviews require at least one steward + one cross-team reviewer for collections marked "high impact." Store review decisions and link to PR/drive artifacts.
5) CI/CD & gating: allow model/config rollout pipelines to reference a collection snapshot id. When a rollout is proposed, CI runs the evals against the referenced snapshot (and optionally a canary subset). If any metric crosses configurable delta thresholds, the pipeline fails and posts a detailed regression report.
6) Regression detection & reporting: standardized metric set, baseline capture semantics, delta thresholds, confidence estimation (bootstrap or sample-size-aware), and a regression report template (summary + examples + metric diffs + suggested rollback). Push reports to Console, Slack, and create a ticket stub when high-impact regressions occur.
7) Console UX: Collection explorer (search, filter by tag/owner), version timeline, diff view between versions (with sample input/output diffs), permissions panel, and quick attach button to point a rollout to a snapshot.
8) Migration plan: import existing curated sets (map IDs, dedupe prompts, assign temporary stewards), add provenance tags for legacy collections.
9) Auditing: every run and user action must be logged with digest references for forensic replay.

Implementation notes & trade-offs:
- Storage: prefer immutable S3 objects keyed by hash + metadata entries in our metadata DB for lookups. Trade-off is eventual additional storage cost vs. traceability.
- Comparison/diffing: full diff for small collections; sampled diff and token-level stats for very large collections to keep UI responsive.
- Approvals: lightweight default path for low-impact collections, stricter path for "high impact" to avoid blocking rapid iteration.
- Auto-eval cadence: allow teams to opt into a continuous background run (daily/hourly) vs. per-rollout on-demand. Background runs increase infra cost but catch regressions earlier.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Product: Console allows creation of a collection, produces an immutable snapshot id, and shows the version history with user/changelog.
- Security: Collection permissions honor SSO group-to-role mappings; unauthorized users cannot attach a snapshot to a rollout.
- CI integration: A rollout pipeline can reference a snapshot id; CI runs the evals and fails the rollout if threshold exceeded. Example PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ci-config/pull/273 (spec).
- Reporting: Regression report contains metric deltas, 10 representative input-output examples, and links to the collection snapshot and run logs.
- Migration: At least 90% of existing curated prompt collections are successfully imported with owner assigned and provenance tags.

Telemetry & Metrics to track success:
- % of rollouts that reference a snapshot (goal: 80% within 3 months of launch)
- # of false-positive regression alerts (goal: reduce by 50% vs baseline after 1 month)
- Time-to-detect regression from deployment (goal: < 15 minutes for CI-gated runs)

Stakeholders & reviewers:

Links & artifacts:
- Draft spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Reference+Collections+Spec
- UX mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/ref-collections-mockups
- CI gating design doc: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/blob/main/ci-gating.md

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (MVP, 4 weeks): metadata model, immutable snapshots, Console create/list/version, API to attach snapshot to rollout (on-demand eval).
Phase 2 (8 weeks): review workflow, RBAC integration, CI gating and regression reports, basic diff view.
Phase 3 (ongoing): migration of legacy collections, background continuous runs, advanced diffs and sampling heuristics, audit exports.

Risks:
- High infra cost for frequent background evals; mitigate with sampling, cold/hot flags, and quotas.
- False regressions due to dataset flakiness; mitigate by adding stability/flakiness score per test and configurable grace windows.

Open questions:
- What is the default retention period for snapshots before archival? (suggest 1 year active, then cold archival)
- Should we provide a managed dedup/normalization tool for prompt canonicalization or leave that to stewards?
- Who owns the cross-team "steward" role definition?
